STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.speaker: A minority
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.claim: A minority classifies most of the surah as Madinan but verses 68–70 as Makkan.
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.anchor: while a minority consider most of the sūrah to be from the Madinan period and vv. 68–70 to be from the Makkan period

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p356/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p356/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p356/r2.claim: Verses 35-44 invoke earlier messengers and rejecters to encourage patience; rejecters are worse than animals and enslaved to desire, while the Prophet must convey truth rather than force acceptance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p356/r2.anchor: A brief reference to the history of messengers and their rejecters to urge the Prophet (sws) and his companions to be patient.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p381/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p381/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p381/r1.claim: A person enslaved to desire exceeds natural limits and becomes worse than an animal.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p381/r1.anchor: he crosses all limits of his instincts and nature

ASAD-NOTES:25:43#n37/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:25:43#n37/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:25:43#n37/r1.claim: Asad glosses “even less conscious of the right way” as being farther astray from the path of truth, linking 7:179.
ASAD-NOTES:25:43#n37/r1.anchor: Lit., "they are farther astray from the path [of truth]": see note 144 on 7:179.

ELMALILI:25:43-44/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r7.claim: Most neither heed transmitted evidence nor act through rational evidence.
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r7.anchor: ne delîl-i sem‘î tanır söz dinlerler, ne de delîl-i aklî tanır akıl ile hareket ederler

ELMALILI:25:43-44/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r8.claim: They resemble cattle because they do not use reason or hearing and follow only their sensations.
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r8.anchor: akl ü sem‘e göre hareket etmez, mücerred hissiyâtlarına tâbi‘olurlar

ELMALILI:25:43-44/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r9.claim: Cattle obey their keepers, distinguish benefactors from those who harm them, seek benefit, avoid harm, and know their food and familiar routes.
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r9.anchor: en‘âm, ehlî hayvanlar bakanlarına inkıyad ederler, kendilerine iyilik edenlerle

ELMALILI:25:43-44/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r10.claim: Cattle use their given faculties as intended and lack beliefs in both good and evil, whereas these people fail even to recognize their Lord and repay His favors with ingratitude.
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r10.anchor: Kendilerine verilmiş olan kuvvetleri ta‘tîl etmez, mâ-hulika-lehine sarf eder, hak ve hayır akidesi yoksa zulm ü şer akidesi de yoktur. Onlar ise Rablerini tanımazlar, O’nun ihsanlarına karşı nankörlük ederler

ELMALILI:25:43-44/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r11.claim: They reject eternal reward and fail to avoid punishment, betray even their homeland, corrupt human nature, foment discord, and disorder the world through oppression, corruption, deception, and seduction.
ELMALILI:25:43-44/r11.anchor: ebedî menfaat olan sevâbı istemez, en büyük zarar olan ikābdan korunmazlar, vatanlarına bile hıyanet ederler. Fıtratı bozmaya, fitneler çıkarmaya çalışır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r2.claim: The Qur'an opposes the mindset that deifies base desires; while people persist in it, they cannot understand the Prophet's call or reason soundly and are more astray than animals.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r2.anchor: putperestlerin, bayağı arzularını tanrı edinmeyi sürdürdükçe Peygamber’in davetini doğru anlamalarının, akıllarını kullanarak sağlıklı değerlendirme yapmalarının imkânsız olduğu bildirilmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r3.claim: These verses criticize Meccan polytheists while teaching a universal lesson: across history, people wrongly rank bodily desires, material interests, and status above reason, sound belief, and justice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r3.anchor: insanlığın temel sorunu, bedensel arzularını, maddî çıkarlarını, makam ve mevki tutkularını akıl ve irfanın ışığından, doğru inanç ve sağlıklı düşünceden, hak ve adalet ölçülerine göre hüküm ve karar verip hayatlarını bu ölçülerle düzenlemekten daha önemli görmeleridir.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p375/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p375/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p375/r4.claim: The Moses and Noah narratives and intervening peoples assure the Prophet and warn his nation: earlier communities mocked messengers who taught them and ultimately suffered a terrible fate; the next sūrah gives these events in detail.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p375/r4.anchor: The purpose is to assure the Prophet (sws) and warn his nation that God sent His teachings to these nations as well.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r4.claim: These verses reassure the Prophet: intellect guides, while desire enslaves, and those who abandon intellect cannot be guided.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r4.anchor: It is a person’s intellect that guides him and not his desire. None can guide people who forsake their intellect and become slaves of their desire.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r7.claim: The question addresses the Prophet, who was exerting himself to reform people, and asks whether he expects them still to understand.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r7.anchor: The words “Do you think that most of them hear or understand?” address the Prophet (sws) who was expending all his efforts to reform these people.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r8.claim: They have squandered their capacity to understand and become like animals, indeed worse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r8.anchor: They have wasted away this faculty and now have become animals; in fact, even worse.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r9.claim: The comparison is precise rather than hyperbolic: animals follow the instincts God created in them without deviation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r9.anchor: Animals follow their instincts on which God has created them and do not deviate from them the slightest.

BURSEVI:v6p158/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p158/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BURSEVI:v6p158/r1.claim: Some commentators hold that this verse was abrogated by the sword verse.
BURSEVI:v6p158/r1.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين : هذه منسوخة بآية السيف.

BURSEVI:v6p158/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p158/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p158/r2.claim: “Do you suppose” means “rather, do you think”; true hearing is hearing the recited signs, while understanding means grasping their admonitions and calls to virtue.
BURSEVI:v6p158/r2.anchor: من المواعظ الزاجرة عن القبائح الداعية إلى المحاسن

BURSEVI:v6p158/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p158/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p158/r3.claim: “Most” is specified because some did believe or recognize the truth but resisted it to protect their leadership.
BURSEVI:v6p158/r3.anchor: وتخصيص الأكثر لأنه كان منهم من آمن ومنهم من عقل الحق وكابر استدبارا وخوفا على الرياسة

BURSEVI:v6p158/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p158/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v6p158/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says a caller’s words reach people only if they heard the primordial call; their response to the prophet is a blessing of that pre-eternal response, while heedlessness reflects their distance from its source.
BURSEVI:v6p158/r4.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : لا تظن أنك تسمع نداءك إنما تسمعهم إن سمعوا نداء الأزل

BURSEVI:v6p158/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p158/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p158/r5.claim: They resemble livestock because they gain no benefit from revealed warnings or observed proofs, remaining heedless and misguided.
BURSEVI:v6p158/r5.anchor: ما يقرع آذانهم من قوارع الآيات وانتفاء التدبر فيما يشاهدونه من الدلائل والمعجزات {إلا كالانعام}

BURSEVI:v6p158/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p158/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p158/r6.claim: The Najmī Interpretations says their only appetite is food, drink, and satisfying the ego’s desires, like livestock.
BURSEVI:v6p158/r6.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : ليس لهم نهمة إلا في الأكل والشرب واستجلاب حظوظ النفس كالبهائم

BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r1.claim: Livestock follow whoever guides them, recognize benefactors, seek what helps, and avoid what harms; these people neither submit to their Lord nor distinguish His beneficence from Satan’s harm, seek reward, or avoid punishment.
BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r1.anchor: لأنها تنقاد لمن يقودها وتميز من يحسن إليها وتطلب ما ينفعها وتجتنب ما يضرها وهؤلاء لا ينقادون لربهم

BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r2.claim: Animals hold no beliefs and acquire no good or evil, whereas these people do; human ignorance also provokes strife and turns others from the truth.
BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r2.anchor: ولأنها لم تعتقد حقا ولم تكتسب خيرا ولا شرا بخلاف هؤلاء ولأن جهالتها لا تضر بأحد وجهالة هؤلاء تؤدي إلى هيج الفتن وصد الناس عن الحق

BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r3.claim: Animals cannot seek perfection and so are not negligent or blameworthy, whereas people can and are culpable for neglect deserving severe punishment.
BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r3.anchor: ولأنها غير متمكنة من طلب الكمال فلا تقصير منها ولاذم وهؤلاء مقصرون مستحقون أعظم العقاب على تقصيرهم.

BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r4.claim: God created angels with reason, beasts with appetite, and humans with both; when appetite overcomes reason a person is worse than beasts, while reason overcoming appetite makes a person like the angels.
BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r4.anchor: خلق الملائكة وعلى العقل جبلهم وخلق البهائم وركب فيها الشهوة وخلق الإنسان وركب فيه الأمرين أي العقل والشهوة

BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r5.claim: A person who masters his own desires is better than the angels, as the verse about the best of creation states.
BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r5.anchor: ومن كان غالبا على أمره فهو خير من الملائكة كما قال تعالى : {أولئك هم خير البرية} (البين : 7)

BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r6.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r6.claim: The Mathnawi depicts angels as reason and worship without appetite, beasts as appetite without knowledge, and humans as divided between an upward and downward pull.

QIRAAT-ER:25:44:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:25:44:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:25:44:2#1/r1.claim: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read taḥsibu while the other readers use taḥsabu; this Najdī–Ḥijāzī vowel difference leaves the meaning unchanged.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r4.claim: They are more astray than livestock because they possess understanding yet fail to use it to escape punishment, whereas livestock cannot understand their interests; the question expresses astonishment at such ignorance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r4.anchor: ثم ذكر أنهم أضل سبيلا من الأنعام من حيث لهم فهم وتركوا استعماله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r13.claim: أم is disconnected and best parsed as بل plus a hamza: Abū Ḥayyān asks whether the worse reproach is that most have no attentive ear for truth or reason to reflect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r13.anchor: وأم منقطعة تتقدر ببل والهمزة على المذهب الصحيح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r14.claim: The comparison with livestock applies to most, since some were destined for felicity and became Muslim; livestock follow keepers, distinguish kindness from harm, seek benefit, avoid injury, and find pasture and water, while people fail in each respect toward God and truth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109#2/r14.anchor: ونفي ذلك عن أكثرهم لأن فيهم من سبقت له السعادة فأسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p111/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p111/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p111/r1.claim: People fail where livestock succeed: they do not obey their Lord, recognize His kindness, seek the greatest reward, avoid the greatest harm, or find the truth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p111/r1.anchor: وهم لا ينقادون لربهم ولا يعرفون إحسانه إليهم ولا يرغبون في الثواب

ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r1.claim: أم shifts from the preceding objection and denies that the Prophet should think most of them can truly hear or reason, despite his earnest preaching and guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r1.anchor: إضراب وانتقال عن الأنكار المذكور في إنكار حسبانه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم إياهم ممن يسمع أو يعقل

ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r2.claim: The preferred reading asks whether they truly hear the Qur'anic verses or understand the signs in the world and themselves, so that the Prophet should invest hope and care in their faith; hearing comes first because it better suits the context.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r2.anchor: ولما كان الدليل السمعي أهم نظرا للمقام من الدليل العقلي قبل : يسمعون أو يعقلون

ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r3.claim: Another reading asks whether they hear the recited verses or understand the admonitions within them that deter vice and call to virtue, explaining the Prophet's effort to guide them.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : المعنى بل أتحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون حق السماع ما تتلو عليهم من الآيات

ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r4.claim: The pronouns refer to 'who' by its meaning for most of them and by its grammatical form for 'upon them'; plural suits the word 'most,' while an earlier singular treats their shared desire as one.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r4.anchor: فضمير ( أكثرهم ) لمن باعتبار معناه وضمير ( عليه ) له أيضا باعتبار لفظه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r5.claim: The claim that 'most of them' means the unbelievers rather than the antecedent 'who' is rejected because the singular عليه rules it out.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : ضمير ( أكثرهم ) للكفار لا لمن لأن قوله ( تعالى ) عليه ياباه وليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r6.claim: Only most are specified because some later received the prior gift of faith and some heard or understood but resisted from arrogance or fear of losing leadership.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r6.anchor: وتخصيص الأكثر لأن منهم من سبقت له العناية الأزلية بالايمان بعد الاتخاذ المذكور

ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r7.claim: The comparison to cattle begins a new sentence that renews the rebuke, closes off the mistaken hope, and says they fail to benefit from warning verses or contemplate clear signs.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r7.anchor: جملة مستأنفة لتكرير النكير وتأكيده وحسم مادة الحسبان بالمرة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r1.claim: Cattle obey their caretaker, recognize kindness and harm, seek benefit, avoid danger, and find food, water, and shelter, while these people disobey their Creator and fail to recognize his beneficence or Satan's harm.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r1.anchor: لما أنها تنقاد لصاحبها الذي يتعهدها وتعرف من يحسن اليها ومن يسيء اليها

ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r2.claim: Animals pursue benefit and avoid harm, while these people neither seek the great reward nor avoid punishment and fail to follow the true path.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r2.anchor: ولا يطلبون الثواب الذي هو أعظم المنافع ولا يتقون العقاب الذي هو أشد المضار

ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r3.claim: If animals lack true belief that leads to good, they also do not adopt falsehood that produces evil; people instead build false premises and derive harmful rules from them.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r3.anchor: ولأنها إن لم تعتقد حقا مستتبعا لاكتساب الخير لم تعتقد باطلا مستوجبا لاقتراف الشر

ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r4.claim: Animal error affects only themselves, but human ignorance causes strife, corruption, obstruction of right guidance, and disorder among people.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r4.anchor: ولأن أحكام جهالتها وضلالتها مقصورة على أنفسها لاتتعدى إلى أحد

ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r5.claim: Animals use their innate faculties for their proper purposes, whereas these people disable reason and neglect the original human disposition.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r5.anchor: ولأنها غير معطلة لقوة من القوى المودعة فيها بل صارفة لها إلى ما خلقت له

ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r6.speaker: الصوفية وجماعة من الناس
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r6.claim: Some infer from the comparison that animals do not know their Lord; Sufis and others instead hold that animals know and glorify God, treating the comparison as outward language.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r6.anchor: ومن ذهب إلى أنها تعلمه سبحانه وتسبحه كما هو مذهب الصوفية وجماعة من الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r7.claim: An alternative says the comparison concerns failure to benefit from Qur'anic verses and cosmic or personal signs; animal knowledge of God is innate rather than inferential.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r7.anchor: وقيل : المراد إن هم إلا كالأنعام في عدم الانتفاع بالآيات القرآنية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r8.claim: On that view, people are more astray because animals were granted knowledge of God and glorify him through it, while these people were not granted it.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r8.anchor: وكونهم أضل سبيلا من الأنعام من حيث أنها رزقت علما بربها تعالى فهي تسبيحه عز وجل به

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r1.claim: Most do not listen as seekers of understanding or reason about the signs they see.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r1.anchor: {أم تحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون} ما تقول سماع طالب الإفهام، {أو يعقلون} ما يعاينون من الحجج والإعلام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r9.claim: Cattle know their pasture and water and obey their keepers, unlike the unbelievers who do not know truth or obey their Creator.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r9.anchor: لأن البهائم تهتدي لمراعيها ومشاربها وتنقاد لأربابها الذين يتعهدونها، وهؤلاء الكفار لا يعرفون طريق الحق، ولا يطيعون ربهم الذي خلقهم ورزقهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r10.claim: Cattle prostrate and glorify God, whereas the unbelievers do not.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p86/r10.anchor: ولأن الأنعام تسجد وتسبح لله وهؤلاء الكفار لا يفعلون.

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r4.claim: Am means rather: should you think most of them hear or reason, so that signs and arguments might benefit them and you hope for their faith?
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r4.anchor: بل أتحسب. { أن أكثرهم يسمعون أو يعقلون } فتجدي لهم الآيات أو الحجج

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r5.claim: This is a stronger reproach than the preceding one, warranting a shift to it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r5.anchor: وهو أشد مذمة مما قبله حتى حق بالإضراب عنه إليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r6.claim: Most is specified because some believed or recognized the truth but resisted from arrogance or fear of losing leadership.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r6.anchor: وتخصيص الأكثر لأنه كان منهم من آمن ومنهم من عقل الحق وكابر استكبارا وخوفا على الرئاسة

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r7.claim: They resemble cattle because they do not benefit when signs strike their ears and do not reflect on proofs and miracles they witness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r7.anchor: في عدم انتفاعهم بقرع الآيات آذانهم وعدم تدبرهم فيما شاهدوا من الدلائل والمعجزات

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r8.claim: Cattle follow their caretakers, distinguish kindness from harm, seek benefits, and avoid harms; these people do none of that toward their Lord.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r8.anchor: لأنها تنقاد لمن يتعهدها وتميز من يحسن إليها ممن يسيء إليها

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r9.claim: People fail to recognize their Lord's beneficence versus Satan's harm, seek no supreme reward, and do not guard against the worst harm, punishment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r9.anchor: ولا يعرفون إحسانه من إساءة الشيطان

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r10.claim: Unlike people, cattle that neither believe truth nor do good also do not believe falsehood or commit evil.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r10.anchor: ولأنها إن لم تعتقد حقا ولم تكتسب خيرا لم تعتقد باطلا ولم تكتسب شرا

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r11.claim: Animal ignorance harms no one, whereas human ignorance produces strife and turns people away from truth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r11.anchor: ولأن جهالتها لا تضر بأحد وجهالة هؤلاء تؤدي إلى هيج الفتن وصد الناس عن الحق

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r12.claim: Cattle cannot seek perfection and so are not blameworthy; people can, and their failure merits the severest punishment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:43-44/r12.anchor: ولأنها غير متمكنة من طلب الكمال فلا تقصير منها ولا ذم وهؤلاء مقصرون ومستحقون أعظم العقاب

SULAMI:v2p61#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p61#4/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p61#4/r1.claim: People hear the pre-eternal call, not merely a human summons; response to a caller comes from the primordial response to God, while heedlessness reflects distance from that ancient place of answer.
SULAMI:v2p61#4/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : لا تظن انك تسمع بندائك إنما يسمعهم نداء الأزل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r5.claim: The rhetorical question denies that most addressees hear or reason in a way that benefits them and might lead them to return voluntarily.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r5.anchor: أي هؤلاء المدعوين { يسمعون } أي سماع من ينزجر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r6.claim: They resemble cattle in failing to use reason and are even more astray: unlike cattle, they do not heed warnings, thank benefactors, avoid enemies, desire reward, or fear punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r6.anchor: بل هم أضل } اي منها { سبيلا * } لأنهم لا ينزجرون بما يسمعون

BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r7.claim: Their misguidance veils reason; if they believed, the veils would lift and faith would illuminate their sight of subtle meanings and hidden realities.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r7.anchor: بظلال الجبال الشامخة من ضلالهم , ولو آمنوا لانقشعت تلك الحجب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p322/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p322/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p322/r1.claim: Just as physical sight cannot distinguish visible things without sunlight, the intellect's spiritual insight cannot grasp meanings as they are without faith's light; spiritual insight is the soul's eye, as sight is the body's.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p322/r1.anchor: الإنسان - وإن كان بصيرا - لا يميز بين المحسوسات ما لم يشرق عليها نور الشمس

BIQAI-FULL:v5p322/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p322/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p322/r2.claim: God's work in the inward realm illuminates it with the sun of spiritual knowledge just as He works in the outward world, showing how He deprives them of benefit from what He gave them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p322/r2.anchor: ولأن عمله في الباطن ينيره إذا شاء بشمس المعارف كعمله في الظاهر سواء , دليلا على سلبهمالنفع بما أعطاهموه

DURR-FULL:v6p260/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās compares disbelievers to livestock: they hear a command or admonition only as sound and do not understand its meaning.
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {أم تحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون} قال: مثل الذين كفروا كمثل البعير والحمار والشاة

DURR-FULL:v6p260/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r8.speaker: مقاتل
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r8.claim: Muqātil explains 'more astray in the path' to mean that they have missed the way.
DURR-FULL:v6p260/r8.anchor: عن مقاتل في قوله {بل هم أضل سبيلا} قال: أخطأ السبيل

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2700/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2700/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2700/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the disbelievers neither hear nor see guidance nor comprehend it.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2700/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : لا يسمعون الهدى ولا يبصرونه ولا يعقلونه

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2700/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2700/r2.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2700/r2.claim: A previously cited report from Salmān al-Fārisī describes four kinds of hearts and identifies the covered heart as the disbeliever's.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2700/r2.anchor: حديث سلمان الفارسي _ رضي الله عنه _ : القلوب اربعة قلب اغلف فذلك قلب الكافر

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2700/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2700/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2700/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās compares disbelievers to livestock: they hear a voice but do not understand an admonition to do good or avoid evil.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2700/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : مثل الذين كفروا كمثل البعير والحمار والشاة ان قلت لبعضهم كل لم يعلم ما تقول غير انه يسمع صوتك

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2700/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2700/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2700/r4.claim: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān says being more astray means missing the right path.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2700/r4.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان قوله : اضل سبيلا يقول اخطا السبيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r1.claim: The passage moves from despair over their desire-dominated minds to warning against assuming they grasp proofs; the disjunctive am shifts from one denial to another and coordinates an implied question.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r1.anchor: ف { أم } منقطعة للإضراب الانتقالي من إنكار إلى إنكار وهي مؤذنة باستفهام عطفته على الاستفهام الذي قبلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r2.claim: Denying that most hear means they do not understand the truth in the message; one who doubts it is like someone who never heard it, as in the cited analogy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r2.anchor: والمراد من نفي { أن أكثرهم يسمعون } نفي أثر السماع وهو فهم الحق لأن ما يلقيه إليهم الرسول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r3.claim: The alternative of reason concerns nonverbal signs in created things, which they also fail to understand.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r3.anchor: وعطف { أو يعقلون } على { يسمعون } لنفي أن يكونوا يعقلون الدلائل غير المقالية وهي دلائل الكائنات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r4.claim: The verse says most rather than all because ordinary followers lack insight, while some intelligent people read cosmic signs but pride and status keep them from following the Prophet alongside poor and enslaved believers such as ʿAmmār and Bilāl.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r4.anchor: لأن هذا حال دهمائهم ومقلديهم ، وفيهم معشر عقلاء يفهمون ويستدلون بالكائنات ولكنهم غلب عليهم حب الرئاسة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r5.claim: The cattle comparison explains how sound senses can receive the call yet yield no benefit when people are not disposed to attend; it approximates their lack of understanding.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r5.anchor: فكان تشبيههم بالأنعام تبيينا للجمع بين حصول اختراق أصوات الدعوة آذانهم مع عدم انتفاعهم بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r6.claim: Abū al-Ṭayyib's verse illustrates that someone may surpass people while still belonging to their kind; the plural pronouns refer to the majority according to the noun's meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r6.anchor:
كقول أبي الطيب :
فإن تفق الأنام وأنت منهم
فإن المسك بعض دم الغزال
وضمائر الجمع عائدة إلى أكثرهم باعتبار معنى لفظه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r8.claim: They resemble livestock in ignorance of benefits and heedlessness about consequences, yet are worse because they possess understanding and abandon it and stray over more serious matters.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r8.anchor: بل هم كالأنعام في الجهل بالمنافع وقلة التحسس للعواقب،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r9.claim: Livestock cannot understand their interests, whereas these people have understanding but leave it unused.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r9.anchor: لهم الفهم وتركوه، و «الأنعام» لا سبيل لهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#4/r1.claim: The “most of them” are the people of Mecca; hearing means hearing in search of understanding, and reasoning means considering the proofs and signs they see.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#4/r1.anchor: يعني أهل مكة والمراد يسمعون سماع طالب الإفهام أو يعقلون ما يعاينون من الحجج والأعلام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#4/r2.claim: One explanation compares them to livestock because livestock hear a sound but do not understand speech.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#4/r2.anchor: أحدهما أن الأنعام تسمع الصوت ولا تفقه القول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#4/r3.claim: Another explanation compares them to livestock because their only concerns are eating and drinking.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#4/r3.anchor: والثاني أنه ليس لها هم إلا المأكل والمشرب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#4/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#4/r4.claim: They are more astray because livestock find their pastures, obey their owners, and respond to those who treat them kindly, whereas these people do the opposite.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92#4/r4.anchor: لأن البهائم تهتدي لمراعيها وتنقاد لأربابها وتقبل على المحسن إليها وهم على خلاف ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113#2/r3.claim: Most rejecters neither truly hear nor reason and are worse off than grazing livestock: animals fulfill their purpose, while humans were made to worship God alone yet associate partners despite proof and messengers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113#2/r3.anchor: أي: أسوأ حالا من الأنعام السارحة، فإن تلك تعقل ما خلقت له، وهؤلاء خلقوا لعبادة الله وحده لا شريك له، وهم يعبدون غيره ويشركون به، مع قيام الحجة عليهم، وإرسال الرسل إليهم.

NAHHAS:v3p161/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p161/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p161/r13.claim: The wording avoids saying they will not believe because some of them were known to believe.
NAHHAS:v3p161/r13.anchor: ولم يقل أنهم لأن منهم من قد علم أنه يؤمن

NAHHAS:v3p161/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p161/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p161/r14.claim: ‘Do they hear?’ means hear with acceptance, and ‘reason’ means reflect on the Prophet’s words and understand them; otherwise they are like those who neither hear nor reason.
NAHHAS:v3p161/r14.anchor: أم تحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون سماع قبول أو يفكرون فيما تقوله فيعقلونه

NAHHAS:v3p161/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p161/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p161/r15.claim: Another explanation is that they gain no benefit from what they hear, so it is as though they had not heard.
NAHHAS:v3p161/r15.anchor: وقيل المعنى أنهم لما ينتفعوا بما يسمعون فكأنهم لم يسمعوا

NAHHAS:v3p161/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p161/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p161/r16.claim: They do not understand like livestock; they are even further astray because they deny the truth they hear, unlike livestock.
NAHHAS:v3p161/r16.anchor: أي إنهم لا يفهمون ( بل هم أضل سبيلا ) لأنهم يكذبون بما يسمعون

MUQATIL:25:44/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:25:44/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:25:44/r1.claim: Most do not hear or understand guidance and resemble cattle absorbed in eating and drinking without regard for the afterlife.
MUQATIL:25:44/r1.anchor: { أم تحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون } إلى الهدى { أو يعقلون } الهدى، ثم شبههم بالبهائم، فقال سبحانه: { إن هم إلا كالأنعام }

MUQATIL:25:44/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:25:44/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:25:44/r2.claim: They are more astray than cattle, which recognize and remember their Lord, whereas the Meccan unbelievers do not know Him to affirm His oneness.
MUQATIL:25:44/r2.anchor: { بل هم أضل سبيلا } [آية: 44] يقول: بل هم أخطأ طريقا من البهائم، لأنها تعرف ربها وتذكره،

NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r1.claim: The disconnected am means rather, shifting from the prior rebuke to a stronger one: they lack hearing for truth and reason for reflection.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r1.anchor: أم منقطعة معناه بل أتحسب كأن هذه المذمة أشد من التى تقدمتها حتى حقت بالاضراب عنها اليها وهى كونهم مسلوبى الاسماع والعقول

NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r2.claim: They resemble livestock in heedlessness and misguidance, and Satan has mastered them because they abandoned inference.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r2.anchor: لانهم لا يلقون إلى استماع الحق أذنا ولا إلى تدبره عقلا ومشبهين بالانعام التى هى مثل فى الغفلة والضلالة فقد ركبهم الشيطان بالاستدلال لتركهم الاستدلال

NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r3.claim: They are more astray than livestock: animals praise and obey their Lord and feeder, recognize beneficence, seek benefit, avoid harm, and find pasture, while these people reject God and fail to pursue reward, avoid punishment, or find truth.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r3.anchor: ثم هم ارجح ضلالة منها لأن الانعام تسبح ربها وتسجد له وتطيع من يعلفها وتعرف من يحسن اليها ممن يسئ اليها وتطلب ما ينفعها وتجتنب ما يضرها وتهتدى لمراعيها ومشاربها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r4.claim: A reported scheme assigns spirit and reason to angels, soul and desire to beasts, and all of these to humans; if desire rules, beasts surpass humans, but if reason rules, angels do.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r4.anchor: وقالوا للملائكة روح وعقل والبهائم نفس وهوى والآدمى مجمع الكل ابتلاء فان غلبته النفس والهوى فضلته الانعام وان غلبته الروح والعقل فضل الملائكة الكرام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r5.claim: The verse says most because some were deterred from Islam only by love of leadership, and some did believe.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170#4/r5.anchor: ذكر الاكثر لأن فيهم من لم يصده عن الإسلام إلا حب الرياسة وكفى به داء عضالا ولأن فيهم من آمن

QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r1.claim: The wording says ‘most’ rather than ‘all’ because God knew that some among them would believe.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r1.anchor: ولم يقل أنهم لأن منهم من قد علم أنه يؤمن

QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r2.claim: Their hearing would mean listening receptively, or reflecting on the Prophet’s words and understanding them; in practice they are as if deaf and unreasoning.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r2.anchor: سماع قبول أو يفكرون فيما تقول فيعقلونه أي هم بمنزلة من لا يعقل ولا يسمع

QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r3.claim: Because they gain no benefit from what they hear, it is as though they did not hear; the intended people are the Meccans.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r3.anchor: لما لم ينتفعوا بما يسمعون فكأنهم لم يسمعوا والمراد أهل مكة

QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r4.claim: Here أَمْ has the sense of بل (rather).
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r4.anchor: قيل: { أم } بمعنى بل في مثل هذا الموضع

QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r5.claim: They resemble cattle in eating and drinking, without reflecting on the Hereafter.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r5.anchor: أي في الأكل والشرب لا يفكرون في الآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r6.claim: They are further astray because cattle face neither reckoning nor punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r6.anchor: إذ لا حساب ولا عقاب على الأنعام

QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r7.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r7.claim: Animals recognize their Lord, find their pastures, and obey their handlers, while these people neither obey nor recognize their Creator and Provider.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل: البهائم تعرف ربها وتهتدي إلى مراعيها وتنقاد لأربابها

QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r8.claim: Animals cannot reason out the truth of monotheism and prophethood, but they also do not believe those truths false.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:44/r8.anchor: لأن البهائم إن لم تعقل صحة التوحيد والنبوة لم تعتقد بطلان ذلك أيضا

RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r8.claim: The disconnected “am” means “rather”; it shifts to a harsher rebuke because their stubbornness keeps them from listening or reflecting, so they are likened to animals that do not benefit from speech or thought.
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r8.anchor: ثالثها : قوله : { أم تحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون أو يعقلون } أم ههنا منقطعة ، معناه بل تحسب

RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r9.claim: “Most” is specified because some knew God and the truth but left Islam from love of leadership rather than ignorance.
RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r9.anchor: والجواب : لأنه كان فيهم من يعرف الله تعالى ويعقل الحق ، إلا أنه ترك الإسلام لمجرد حب الرياسة لا للجهل .

RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r1.claim: Animals obey their keepers, distinguish kindness from harm, and seek benefits; these people disobey their Lord, mistake Satan’s harm for good, and shun reward while ignoring punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r1.anchor: أن الأنعام تنقاد لأربابها وللذي يعلفها ويتعهدها وتميز بين من يحسن إليها وبين من يسيء إليها

RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r2.claim: Animals lack both knowledge and false belief, whereas these people lack knowledge, are ignorant of their own ignorance, and persist in thinking they know.
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r2.anchor: ثانيها : أن قلوب الأنعام كما أنها تكون خالية عن العلم فهي / خالية عن الجهل الذي هو اعتقاد المعتقد على خلاف ما هو عليه مع التصميم .

RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r3.claim: Animals’ ignorance harms no one, but human ignorance causes great harm because they obstruct God’s path and seek to make it crooked.
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r3.anchor: وثالثها : أن عدم علم الأنعام لا يضر بأحد أما جهل هؤلاء فإنه منشأ للضرر العظيم ، لأنهم يصدون الناس عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا

RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r4.claim: Animals cannot pursue higher ranks, while people can; a person who chooses to abandon attainable excellence deserves more blame than one unable to seek it.
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r4.anchor: ورابعها : أن الأنعام لا تعرف شيئا ولكنهم عاجزون عن الطلب وأما هؤلاء الجهال فإنهم ليسوا عاجزين عن الطلب ، والمحروم عن طلب المراتب العالية إذا عجز عنه لا يكون في استحقاق الذم كالقادر عليه التارك له لسوء اختياره

RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r5.claim: Beasts are not punished for lack of knowledge, while these people deserve the greatest punishment for theirs.
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r5.anchor: وخامسها : أن البهائم لا تستحق عقابا على عدم العلم ، أما هؤلاء فإنهم يستحقون عليه أعظم العقاب

RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r6.claim: Some hold that beasts glorify God, as these verses say; on that account the disbelievers’ error is even greater than the animals’.
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r6.anchor: وسادسها : أن البهائم تسبح الله تعالى على مذهب بعض الناس على ما قال { وإن من شىء إلا يسبح بحمده } ( الأسراء : 44 )

RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r7.claim: Their lack of hearing and reason means they fail to use those faculties, not that they literally lack intellect; this is like calling someone blind or deaf when he does not understand.
RAZI-FULL:v24p76/r7.anchor: الجواب : ليس المراد أنهم لا يعقلون بل إنهم لا ينتفعون بذلك العقل ، فهو كقول الرجل لغيره إذا لم يفهم إنما أنت أعمى وأصم .

STUDYQURAN:25:44/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:44/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:25:44/r1.claim: Disbelievers resemble cattle because they do not think and limit their concerns to eating and drinking; unlike humans, cattle are not condemned for this.
STUDYQURAN:25:44/r1.anchor: they do not think and restrict their concerns to eating and drinking; they are even further astray

STUDYQURAN:25:44/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:44/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:25:44/r2.claim: Cattle follow their natures, obey herders, and can hear and understand as animals, while disbelievers disobey God and lack ears and eyes for truth.
STUDYQURAN:25:44/r2.anchor: cattle follow their natures, know how to obey their herders, and can hear and understand insofar as they are animals

STUDYQURAN:25:44/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:44/r3.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:25:44/r3.claim: Cattle lack knowledge but do not have the compound ignorance of neither knowing nor knowing that they do not know.
STUDYQURAN:25:44/r3.anchor: they are not guilty of the compound ignorance of both not knowing and not knowing that they do not know

STUDYQURAN:25:44/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:44/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:25:44/r4.claim: Cattle know what benefits or harms them, whereas some people fail to recognize God’s goodness and Satan as enemy, and so cannot seek the Hereafter’s good and avoid punishment.
STUDYQURAN:25:44/r4.anchor: Cattle, moreover, know what is good and bad for them, whereas some human beings do not understand how good God has been to them

STUDYQURAN:25:44/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:44/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:25:44/r5.claim: Other Quranic comparisons of people to animals appear at the listed verses.
STUDYQURAN:25:44/r5.anchor: Other verses that compare human beings to animals include 2:65; 7:176; 29:41

TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r1.claim: A pagan who takes desire as god worships whichever idol he chooses; if he sees a better stone, he abandons the first and worships the new one.
TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r1.anchor: فكان معبوده وإلهه ما يتخيره لنفسه

TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r2.claim: Muhammad is not a guardian over such a person’s acts, given the person’s great ignorance.
TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r2.anchor: أفأنت تكون يا محمد على هذا حفيظا في أفعاله مع عظيم جهله

TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r3.claim: The pagans do not hear the recitation in a way that lets them understand it or grasp God's proofs.
TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r3.anchor: يا محمد أن أكثر هؤلاء المشركين {يسمعون} [البقرة: 75] ما يتلى عليهم، فيعون {أو يعقلون} [الفرقان: 44] ما يعاينون من حجج الله فيفهمون

TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r4.claim: They are worse off than cattle: animals find pasture and obey their masters, but these disbelievers reject their Lord, fail to thank Him, and disobey their Creator.
TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r4.anchor: بل هم من البهائم أضل سبيلا؛ لأن البهائم تهتدي لمراعيها، وتنقاد لأربابها، وهؤلاء الكفرة لا يطيعون ربهم

TABATABAI:25:43-44/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:43-44/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:43-44/r4.claim: Am is disjunctive, hisab means supposition, and the plural pronouns refer semantically to the relative clause in the previous verse.
TABATABAI:25:43-44/r4.anchor: أم منقطعة، والحسبان بمعنى الظن وضمائر الجمع راجعة إلى الموصول في الآية السابقة باعتبار المعنى.

TABATABAI:25:43-44/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:43-44/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:43-44/r5.claim: People reach life's felicity either by reasoning to recognize and follow truth or, if unable to reason independently, by hearing and following someone who knows and advises them.
TABATABAI:25:43-44/r5.anchor: وسيلة الإنسان إلى سعادة الحياة أحد أمرين إما أن يستقل بالتعقل فيعقل الحق فيتبعه أو يرجع إلى قول من يعقله وينصحه

TABATABAI:25:44-46/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:44-46/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:44-46/r1.claim: The question asks whether most can hear truth or reason it out and follow it; the answer explains that they do neither, like livestock that cannot grasp meaning beyond sounds.
TABATABAI:25:44-46/r1.anchor: بل أتظن أن أكثرهم لهم استعداد استماع الحق ليتبعه أو استعداد عقل الحق ليتبعه

TABATABAI:25:44-46/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:44-46/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:44-46/r2.claim: They are more astray than livestock because animals avoid what harms them, while these people prefer harm to benefit; animals also lack the human equipment for guidance that people possess.
TABATABAI:25:44-46/r2.anchor: وذلك أن الأنعام لا تقتحم على ما يضرها وهؤلاء يرجحون ما يضرهم على ما ينفعهم

TABATABAI:25:44-46/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:44-46/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:25:44-46/r3.claim: Some infer from the comparison that livestock have no knowledge of their Lord.
TABATABAI:25:44-46/r3.anchor: واستدل بعضهم بالآية على أن الأنعام لا علم لها بربها

TABATABAI:25:44-46/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:44-46/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:44-46/r4.claim: Tabatabai says the verse denies neither basic knowledge of God in livestock nor in disbelievers; it denies disbelievers' following innate rational truth, which desire has veiled, and compares them with livestock lacking that kind of perception.
TABATABAI:25:44-46/r4.anchor: إن الآية لا تنفي عنها ولا عن الكفار أصل العلم بالله وإنما تنفي عن الكفار اتباع الحق الذي يهدي إليه عقل الإنسان الفطري

TABATABAI:25:44-46/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:44-46/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:25:44-46/r5.claim: Another answer says the wording speaks only according to outward appearance; Tabatabai says that claim cannot be established by argument.
TABATABAI:25:44-46/r5.anchor: وأما ما أجاب به بعضهم أن الكلام خارج مخرج الظاهر فقول لا سبيل إلى إثباته بالاستدلال

ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r5.claim: They resemble cattle in lacking discernment about the signs and proofs presented to them.
ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r5.anchor: معناه ما هم إلا كالأنعام في قلة التمييز فيما جعل دليلا لهم من الآيات والبرهان

ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r6.claim: They are even more astray because cattle praise and prostrate to God, while these people’s hearts are as hard as stones or harder, as in 2:74.
ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r6.anchor: تسبح بحمد الله وتسجد له وهم كما قال الله عز وجل

TABRISI:25:43-45/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:43-45/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:43-45/r6.claim: They do not hear with a learner's intent or reason through Muhammad's recitation and the miracles and proofs they witness.
TABRISI:25:43-45/r6.anchor: ما يعاينونه من المعجزات والحجج أي لا تظن ذلك

TABRISI:25:43-45/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:43-45/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:43-45/r7.claim: They are like livestock, which hear a call but do not understand it.
TABRISI:25:43-45/r7.anchor: أي ما هم إلا كالبهائم التي تسمع النداء ولا تعقل

TABRISI:25:43-45/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:43-45/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:43-45/r8.claim: They are worse than livestock because people were enabled to know the truth but failed to know it, unlike animals.
TABRISI:25:43-45/r8.anchor: من الأنعام لأنهم مكنوا من المعرفة فلم يعرفوا والأنعام لم يمكنوا منها

TABRISI:25:43-45/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:43-45/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:43-45/r9.claim: Livestock are instinctively guided away from harm, whereas people know the ways of ruin and salvation yet pursue ruin and shun salvation.
TABRISI:25:43-45/r9.anchor: ولأن الأنعام ألهمت منافعها ومضارها فهي لا تفعل ما يضرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r1.claim: أم تحسب means rather, do you think, Muhammad; أكثرهم refers to Meccans, and hearing is listening to understand while عقل is distinguishing guidance from error.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r1.anchor: بل أتحسب يا محمد (¬3) {أن أكثرهم} (¬4) # قال ابن عباس: يريد أهل مكة في {يسمعون}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r2.claim: Muqatil says they resemble livestock in eating and drinking and pay no attention to the afterlife.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: في الأكل والشرب، لا يلتفتون إلى الآخرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi says they resemble livestock in food and drink, understanding nothing beyond that.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي: شبههم بالأنعام في المأكل والمشرب لا تعقل غيره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the comparison concerns their poor discernment of the signs and proofs set before them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: في قلة التمييز فيما جعل دليلا لهم من الآيات، والبرهان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says humans are more astray because livestock receive neither reward nor punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد أن البهائم ليس عليها عقاب ولا لها ثواب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r6.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi's parallel explanation is that livestock have no burden of proof or accountability.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r6.anchor: وهذا معنى قول الكلبي؛ لأنها لا حجة عليها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r7.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r7.claim: Muqatil says the Meccans are more mistaken than livestock, which know and remember their Lord, whereas the Meccans do not recognize and affirm God's oneness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r7.anchor: قال مقاتل: يقول الله: بل هم أخطأ طريقا من البهائم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r8.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj similarly says livestock glorify God and prostrate, while the unbelievers are like rocks or harder, as in 2:74.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r8.anchor: وهذا المعنى أراد الزجاج؛ فقال: لأن الأنعام تسبح بحمد الله، وتسجد له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r9.speaker: قول غير مسمى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r9.claim: Another explanation says animals obey the owners who feed and care for them, while unbelievers neither know truth nor obey their Creator and provider.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r9.anchor: وقيل: لأن الأنعام تنقاد لأربابها الذين يعلفونها ويتعهدونها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r10.claim: The author notes a parallel to this verse in Surat al-Araf.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p514/r10.anchor: ونظير هذه الآية في سورة الأعراف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:44-47/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:44-47/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:44-47/r1.claim: Most of them hear without understanding and do not reason in their hearts about the message; they resemble livestock in ignorance of signs and evidence.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:44-47/r1.anchor: أكثرهم يسمعون } سماع تفهيم { أو يعقلون } بقلوبهم ما تقول لهم:

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:44-47/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:44-47/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:44-47/r2.claim: They are worse than livestock because livestock follow their caretaker, whereas these people disobey their beneficent master.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:44-47/r2.anchor: لأن النعم تنقاد لمن يتعهده، وهم لا يطيعون مولاهم الذي أنعم عليهم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483#2/r1.claim: The people who think the majority of the polytheists hear or reason are referring to that group; they are like the livestock involved in their worship and even further astray.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483#2/r1.anchor: قوله: {أم تحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون أو يعقلون} [الفرقان: 44] يعني جماعة المشركين. {إن هم إلا كالأنعام} [الفرقان: 44] مما تعبدوا به. {بل هم أضل سبيلا} [الفرقان: 44]

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.claim: Accusative curses such as تربا وجندلا omit a verb; the expression means may God afflict you with dust and stones, and substitutes for تربت يداك and جندلت.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.anchor: تفسيرها ههنا كتفسيرها فى الباب الأول

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.claim: Some Arabs raise ترب and جندل as a subject with a following predicate; the poetic line preserves the same curse meaning as the accusative construction.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.anchor: وقد رفعه بعض العرب فجعله مبتدأ

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.claim: The formula فاها لفيك means a calamity or disaster for you; its wording replaces the verbal phrase دهاك الله, with the verb understood.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.anchor: كأنه قال تربا لفيك فصار بدلا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.speaker: أبو سدرة الهجمي
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.claim: Abū Sidrah al-Hujaymī supplies poetry illustrating the formula فاها لفيك; Sībawayh says a trusted source transmitted the lines.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.anchor: وقال أبو سدرة الهجمي # % تحسب هواس وأقبل

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.claim: A line by ʿĀmir ibn al-Aḥwaṣ describes a calamity as having a mouth, confirming the sense of فاها as a disaster formula.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإ.anchor: وداهية من دواهى المنون % ترهبها الناس

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.claim: A following enclitic hā may be transparent: a nearby kasra pulls the preceding alif toward imāla, as though the hā were absent.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.claim: The closer the kasra is to the alif, the stronger the case for imāla; a hā between them does not prevent it.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.anchor: حرف فهي إذا لم يكن بين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.claim: Speakers also imāle alif near yāʾ, as in بيني وبينها; yāʾ can motivate the shift just as kasra does.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.claim: A ḍamma between alif and kasra blocks imāla in raised forms such as يكيلها, unlike the accusative environment.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.anchor: حاجزا فمنعت الإمالة لأن الباء في قولك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.claim: Without a nearby yāʾ or kasra, forms such as يعلمها and يخفها do not attract imāla.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.anchor: لأنه ليست ههنا ياء ولا كسرة تميل الألف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.claim: A nearby yāʾ triggers imāla in forms such as فينا and علينا; speakers likewise use it in رأيت يدا and بيني وبينها.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.anchor: وعلينا فأمالوا للياء حيث قربت من الألف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.claim: Alif in دما and دمها is not imāled because neither a kasra nor a yāʾ provides the trigger.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.anchor: وقال هؤلاء رأيت دما ودمها فلم يميلوا لأنه لا كسرة فيه ولا ياء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.claim: The hā in عندها does not block imāla because عند itself would be imāled; the hā is treated as absent.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.anchor: لأنه لو قال عند أمال فلما جاءت الهاء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.speaker: بنو تميم
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.claim: Banu Tamim, and also some Qays and Asad speakers, use forms such as رأيت عدا and هو منا; Sībawayh treats these as dialectal patterns.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.anchor: وهم بنو تميم ويقوله أيضا قوم من قيس

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.claim: Arab imāla systems differ: one speaker may imāle forms another leaves open, and this variation is not defective mixing.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.anchor: واعلم أنه ليس كل من أمال الألفات

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.claim: Speakers whose dialect avoids imāla in the earlier categories avoid it throughout this category too.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.anchor: لا يميلون شيئا منها في هذا الباب

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.claim: Imāla spreads leftward: when an alif is imāled, the preceding material is imāled too, including the material before a hā treated as absent.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.claim: Some who imāle يدا leave يدها un-imāled because fatha dominates and the yāʾ before dāl is not treated like a weak alif.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.anchor: تكون الفتحة أغلب وصارت الياء بمنزلة دال دم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.claim: Most of the stronger imāla group leave رمى un-imāled, avoiding a movement toward yāʾ; unlike حبلى and معزى, its alif is not a substitute for yāʾ.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.anchor: إمالة رمى فلم يمل كره أن ينحو نحو الياء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.claim: Some imāle the hā-pronoun forms only at pause; in connected speech they restore alif because it is clearer, though others retain imāla in connection.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.anchor: أرادوا في الوقف إذ كانت الألف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.claim: Some Arabs occasionally imāle forms with no regular trigger, treating word-final alif like the alif in حبلى; Sībawayh says this is rare.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.anchor: وقد قال قوم فأمالوا أشياء ليست فيها علة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.claim: Some speakers leave عبدا and عنبا open when strong consonants separate the kasra from alif; imāla in عمادا and معزانا is analogical where kasra is stronger.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.anchor: وهو عندنا فلم يميلوا لأنه وقع

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناس.claim: A kasra that is more firmly present gives a stronger basis for imāla.

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r13.claim: Hearing means attentive listening for understanding, and reasoning means grasping proofs and miracles they witness.
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r13.anchor: أي: سماع طالب للإفهام، ويعقلون ما يعاينون من الحجج والمعجزات

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r14.claim: One comparison is that they hear but do not understand or reason about visible proofs, like livestock.
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r14.anchor: قال: يعني ما هم إلا كالأنعام، يعني تسمع ولا تفهم ولا تعقل ما ترى من الحجج

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r15.claim: Another comparison is that they are absorbed in appetites, eating, and enjoyment.
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r15.anchor: وقيل: هم كالأنعام مشتغلون بالشهوات والأكل والتمتع

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r16.claim: People are more astray because they could acquire knowledge but did not, while animals lack that capacity.
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r16.anchor: قيل: لأنهم تمكنوا من المعرفة فلم يعرفوا، والأنعام لم تتمكن

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r17.claim: Another explanation contrasts humans, who face commands, promises, and threats, with animals, which do not.
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r17.anchor: وقيل: لا خطاب عليها ولا وعد ولا وعيد، وعليكم ذلك

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r18.claim: Another view says animals know what benefits them and obey their owners, unlike unbelievers.
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r18.anchor: وقيل: البهائم تهتدي لصلاحها وتطيع أربابها بخلاف الكفار

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r19.claim: A final explanation says animals do not profess unbelief, whereas these people chose unbelief.
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r19.anchor: وقيل: لأن الأنعام لا تعتقد الكفر وإن لم تعتقد شيئا، وهؤلاء كفروا فهم أضل سبيلا

JISHUMI:v7p5310/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5310/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5310/r3.claim: Listening without seeking understanding and benefit counts as no real hearing.
JISHUMI:v7p5310/r3.anchor: وتدل على أن من يسمع لا للتفهم والفائدة كان كلا سماع

JISHUMI:v7p5310/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5310/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5310/r4.claim: The signs of divine unity are established by recalling God’s many blessings upon servants.
JISHUMI:v7p5310/r4.anchor: وتدل على أن إثبات التوحيد ما عد من الآيات على نعمه تعالى بجميع ذلك على عباده
